headline: Designing Eco-Efficint Biowaste Valorisation Systems: Effects of Transport Distance and Facility Scale
name: Designing Eco-Efficint Biowaste Valorisation Systems: Effects of Transport Distance and Facility Scale
description: The increasing deployment of separate biowaste collection across Europe raises questions regarding environmentally and economically optimal treatment strategies . From this perspective, the balance between decentralised and centralised infrastructure is a potential lever to consider. The choice of technologies is another . Composting and anaerobic digestion (AD) offer viable circular bioeconomy pathways, but their performance depends on transport distance, facility size, seasonal waste fluctuations, and technological efficiency. Threshold distances and scale -dependent interactions affecting the environmental and economic performance of treatment plants remain poorly characterised. This study develops a unified techno -economic and life cycle assessment framework to quantify how transport constraints and treatment capacities shape biowaste valorisation systems. Three facility scales for composting and AD are evaluated across a range of transport distances and compared with local incineration in terms of environmental and economic performance . Transport burdens are modelled using vehicle life cycle assessment (LCA) and realistic heavy -duty truck data for electric -, gas-, and diesel -powered vehicles. Results reveal non-linear trade-offs between scale and transport, with zero-distance composting yielding the lowest combined impacts. Across all scenarios, 45 configurations outperform local incineration economically and environmentally, while 111 remain environmentally preferable despite higher costs, thus providing quantitative guidance for infrastructure planning.

hasPart.name: 1. Introduction
hasPart.description: This section introduces the challenges and regulatory context of biowaste valorisation across Europe, highlighting the need to balance decentralised and centralised infrastructure. It outlines the study's objective to develop a unified framework combining techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment to evaluate treatment pathways.

hasPart.name: 2. Methodology
hasPart.description: This section details the methodological approach used to model the environmental and economic performance of biowaste valorisation systems. It establishes the overall framework for assessing facility scales, transport impacts, and scenario configurations.

hasPart.name: 2.1 Environmental modelling and system boundaries
hasPart.description: This subsection defines the system boundaries and LCA modeling parameters for evaluating the environmental impacts of biowaste treatment and transport. It accounts for vehicle emissions and facility-level processes across different technological setups.

hasPart.name: 2.2 Techno-Economic Analysis
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the economic assessment methods used to calculate capital, operational, and transport costs for centralised and decentralised facilities. It provides the financial framework for comparing valorisation routes against local incineration.

hasPart.name: 2.3 Scenario construction and assumptions
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the specific scenarios, technological parameters, and baseline assumptions formulated for composting, anaerobic digestion, and transport modes. It establishes the variable ranges for facility capacity and hauling distances.

hasPart.name: 3. Results
hasPart.description: This section presents the findings of the techno-economic and environmental assessments, highlighting the performance of various configuration scales and transport distances. It demonstrates how trade-offs manifest across different operational setups.

hasPart.name: 3.1 Cost Implications of a Centralised versus Decentralised System
hasPart.description: This subsection evaluates the economic impact of facility scale and transport distances, comparing the financial viability of centralised plants versus smaller decentralised units. It identifies critical cost thresholds driven by logistics and plant capacity.

hasPart.name: 3.2 Environmental assessment of the configurations
hasPart.description: This subsection analyzes the environmental footprints of the different biowaste treatment configurations, focusing on emissions, energy recovery, and nutrient recycling benefits. It evaluates how transport burdens offset processing advantages.

hasPart.name: 3.3 Cost-Environmental Trade-Offs and Pareto-Optimal configurations
hasPart.description: This subsection synthesizes economic and environmental indicators to identify Pareto-optimal infrastructure configurations. It maps out which systems successfully outperform baseline incineration options across combined metrics.

hasPart.name: 4. Conclusions
hasPart.description: This section summarizes the key findings of the study regarding the non-linear relationship between facility scale and transport distance. It provides final actionable insights for regional planning and biowaste infrastructure deployment.
